Subject: Initial DPA items: EU pinning, subprocessors, and temporary failover windows

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HelixCare is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move to a PO, our legal and security teams asked for a few clarifications on residency and subprocessors so we can finish our DPA questionnaire (attached). High level asks: 

- Can Redwood provide a binding commitment to process HelixCare customer data in the EU (no US egress) for the primary workload?
- If temporary cross-border processing is required (eg. maintenance, failover), can that be limited to a fixed maximum window (we propose 72 hours) and require advance notification and audit logs?
- We need the current subprocessors roster and confirmation that embeddings/analytics telemetry won’t be retained outside the EU.

I attached our questionnaire for your legal ops to complete. We’d like to keep this to a short set of written commitments + a one-hour legal/ops call.

Marta — thanks for the detailed questionnaire and for outlining HelixCare’s constraints. I’ve started answers inline in the doc and pulled a short summary here so we can get to a call quickly. I’ve also attached our current subprocessor roster (csv).

Summary answers (short):
- Regional binding: We can offer EU affinity with routing guarantees for production workloads. Practically, that means requests from HelixCare tenant IDs are routed to EU data centers and processed in-region for normal operations.
- Temporary cross-border windows: We agree to a constrained temporary failover model. Our proposed default is: scheduled maintenance windows or unplanned failover may trigger temporary processing in non-EU regions only when EU capacity is unavailable; we will aim for automated failover to an EU model variant first. We accept a 72-hour maximum contingency window (can be contractually bounded) and will provide audit logs for any cross-border processing event.
- Subprocessors & telemetry: attached roster contains subprocessors and region mappings. Embeddings and analytic telemetry are by default stored in-region; we do not index or store identifiable customer prompt content in US unless explicitly required for debugging, and then only with customer approval.

Next steps: 
1) Laura (legal) — can you review the draft clause in the attached doc and propose DPA redlines?
2) Markus (ops) — can you confirm the KMS/CMK options and transient replication behavior?
3) Marta — would Thursday or Friday next week for a 45-minute call work? Please send preferred times.

Marta / team — quick technical addendum to Soojin’s summary: 

- How EU affinity works: tenant routing uses regional tags on the control plane and data-plane tenancy. For production traffic we route 99.9% of requests to EU compute (primary region). Cache prefixes are stored regionally; KV cache replication is disabled by default for pinned tenants.
- Fallback behavior: we attempt warm-failover to another EU availability zone/region first. Only if capacity constraints or emergency hardware failures leave no EU option will we trigger a controlled temporary replication to a compatible non-EU region. The temporary replica is read-only for session state and is used only for inference; persistent storage (logs, embeddings) is not written out-of-region unless explicitly allowed.
- KMS: we support customer-managed CMKs via our KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) in EU regions — that can prevent any keys from being usable outside the EU region. If HelixCare wants an added escrow-key option for emergency unsealing during a region outage, we can discuss an architecture for that (it’s an add-on).
- Notification & telemetry: we will provide: start/end timestamps for any cross-border event, affected tenant IDs, per-request sampling for audit, and all relevant audit logs.

Operational ask: If HelixCare agrees to the 72-hour maximum, we’ll add automated throttles to enforce a forced re-home attempt at 48 hrs and an escalation to product/ops at 60 hrs.

Subject: Re: Initial DPA items: EU pinning, subprocessors, and temporary failover windows

Marta — looping in Redwood legal. Thank you for the questionnaire. Attached is a narrow draft clause we propose adding to the DPA to capture the temporary cross-border processing commitments discussed below. Key points: 

- "Temporary Cross-Border Processing": limited to a maximum of 72 consecutive hours per incident unless both parties agree in writing to extend; allowed only when EU processing is unavailable; requires written notice to the customer within 24 hours of start; Redwood will provide audit logs and a post-incident report.
- KMS safeguard: if customer uses CMK in an EU KMS, Redwood must not be able to decrypt data outside the EU region unless customer authorizes a temporary unseal; language to permit an escrowed emergency key can be added as an optional exhibit.
- Subprocessor transparency: Redwood will deliver an up-to-date roster before execution and 30 days’ advance notice for onboarding any subprocessor that will handle customer content.

Please review the attached doc (short clause) and let us know whether HelixCare legal can accept in principle or needs redlines. If there are DPA negotiations, we’re happy to schedule a 30–45 minute legal-to-legal call next week.

Attachments: Redwood_TempCrossBorder_clause_draft.docx

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with internal expectations. A few follow-ups before we commit: 

- HelixCare accepts the 72-hour cap in principle but requests Redwood to include an explicit automated re-home attempt at 24 hours (noted) and a manual escalation at 48 hours to HelixCare ops.
- Please confirm that embeddings are not replicated out-of-region under the default settings and that any exception requires HelixCare opt-in.
- Legal accepts Redwood’s draft clause pending 2 small redlines: (1) notification within 12 hours of start (instead of 24), and (2) a requirement that Redwood provide the raw audit logs in a machine-readable format within 5 business days post-event.
